ing: hard-boiled and chopped, for egg butter
st: Bring the rice, [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt to a boil in a heavy pot, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add the milk, stir, and cook on low for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often, until a thick porridge. Cool completely.
Mix the rye flour, [[0.75 cup]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt into a smooth dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 12 balls. Roll each into a very thin oval, about 5 inches long, with a little all-purpose flour.
Spoon porridge into the center of each oval, leaving a border.
Fold the long edges up over the filling and pinch the border into small pleats, leaving the center open.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and bake the pasties on a sheet for 15 minutes until the edges are browned and the filling is spotted.
Brush with melted butter, cover with a cloth for 10 minutes to soften, and top with chopped egg mixed with some butter.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the leek for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the broth, potatoes, carrots and allspice and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 12 minutes until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Add the salmon chunks and simmer gently for 5 minutes until just cooked and flaky, at 145°F (63°C).
Stir in the cream and warm through for 2 minutes without boiling.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper, then stir in most of the dill.
Remove the allspice berries if you can find them, and serve with rye bread and the extra dill.

ing: optional; use water to skip beer
st: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until soft, then drain.
Mash with [[1 tbsp]] butter, the milk and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Pat the meat dry. Heat [[1 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over high heat.
Brown the meat in two batches for 2 to 3 minutes each, stirring, and set aside.
Add the last [[1 tbsp]] butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Return the meat and add the beer or water, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Check that the meat is cooked through at 145°F (63°C).
Serve over mashed potatoes with a spoonful of lingonberry jam.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Cook the onion in [[1 tbsp]] butter for 4 minutes until soft, then cool.
Mix the beef, pork, soaked crumbs, onion, egg, allspice, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper gently until combined.
Roll into balls the size of walnuts.
Brown the meatballs in [[1 tbsp]] butter in batches for 6 minutes, turning, until browned all over.
For the gravy, melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in the same pan and whisk in the flour for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth and cream and simmer 5 minutes, then add [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Return the meatballs and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through at 160°F (71°C). Serve with potatoes and lingonberry jam.

ing: smoked pork hock or ham bone
st: Soak the peas in cold water for 8 hours or overnight if you like, then drain.
Put the peas, pork hock, onion and bay leaf in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water.
Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer partly covered for 90 minutes.
Add the carrots, potato and marjoram and cook another 25 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Lift out the pork and shred the meat, discarding the bone and fat.
Return the meat to the soup and add [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Mash a few peas against the pot for thickness, taste, and adjust.
Serve hot with mustard on the side.

ing: small whole fish (vendace or small trout) or fillets
st: Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, lard and warm water into a firm dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Roll the dough into an oval about 1/4 inch thick.
Season the fish with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Layer half the pork on the dough, then the fish and the rest of the pork. Dot with the butter.
Fold the dough up and over to enclose the filling into a tightly sealed loaf, pinching the seams.
Set seam-side up on a baking sheet and bake 4 hours until the crust is dark and the fish is tender at 145°F (63°C).
Brush with melted butter, wrap in a towel, and rest 30 minutes before cutting. Eat the filling with the crust.
Heat the milk gently in a heavy pot to 175°F (80°C) while stirring.
Add the buttermilk and salt and stir slowly until curds separate from the whey.
Let it stand for 10 minutes without heat, then pour it into a cheesecloth-lined strainer.
Press out the whey, then shape the curds in a lined, shallow dish about 1 inch thick.
Press down under a weight for 30 minutes to remove more whey.
Heat the oven broiler to high. Place the cheese on a baking sheet.
Broil it for 3 to 5 minutes until spotted with dark brown patches.
Cut into wedges and serve warm with whipped cream and jam.
Mix the warm water, yeast and honey in a large bowl and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Stir in the rye flour, bread flour and salt to make a sticky, heavy dough.
Knead with wet hands for 8 minutes. Rye dough stays sticky, so do not add much flour.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 2 hours until puffy.
Shape into a round or loaf and place in a greased pan. Sprinkle with caraway if desired.
Cover and let rise another 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and bake for 15 minutes, then lower to 375°F (190°C) and bake 35 minutes.
The loaf should sound hollow when tapped. Cool completely, at least 1 hour, before slicing.
Whisk the warm milk with the yeast, [[0.5 cup]] sugar and cardamom. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[3 cups]] of the flour and the salt, then mix in the soft butter. Add the remaining flour until it forms a soft dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Roll out into a rectangle about 12 by 20 inches.
Spread with the filling butter and sprinkle with the filling sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly from the long side and cut into 12 triangular wedges. Press the point of each wedge down into the roll to make the rolls.
Place on lined trays, cover and rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and brush with the egg.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until golden and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a 9-inch pie dish.
Rub the butter into the flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and the salt with your fingers until crumbly, then mix in the egg to make a dough.
Press the dough into the dish and up the sides. Chill 20 minutes.
Prick the crust with a fork and bake 12 minutes until pale golden.
Toss the blueberries with the cornstarch and [[0.25 cup]] sugar and spread over the crust.
Whisk the sour cream, filling eggs, remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Pour over the berries and bake 35 minutes until the filling is just set.
Cool completely before slicing, which takes about 1 hour.
Stir the rye flour and malt together in a large oven-safe pot or casserole.
Pour in [[3.5 cups]] boiling water, whisking until smooth.
Cover and let it rest in a warm place for 1 hour so the malt can sweeten it.
Stir in the molasses, orange zest and salt.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C), cover the pot tightly, and bake 3 hours, stirring once halfway.
The mixture should be thick, dark and sweet. Take care not to burn the edges.
Cool completely, then chill for at least 24 hours before serving.
Serve cold with cream and sugar.
